interp_p27_n4_dose_bound.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, Fig. 9 n4
interp_p27_n4_dose_bound.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. A first prescription is ordered only for a dose within the printed start amount of that n4 line: amlodipine 5-10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5-25 mg and indapamide SR 1.5-2.5 mg (the printed range; no separate maximum is printed), and exactly enalapril 5 mg or lisinopril 2.5 mg (the one printed start dose; no other first amount is printed). A first dose above the printed start dose and at most the printed Max (enalapril 20 mg, lisinopril 40 mg) goes to clinical review (gap_p27_n4_start_dose). A dose of 0 mg or less, below the lowest printed start amount, or above the highest printed amount, is not a printed dose: it is kept as a refused choice, and the clinician is asked again. A lower first dose (for example for an older patient) therefore has no ordering path; the clinician may choose no n4 medicine. For captopril, losartan and nifedipine SR every positive dose goes to clinical review (gap_p27_n4_maximum); their printed start amounts are recorded but not checked. The frequency is the printed od or bid. Independent review M1, M2 and M4.

interp_p27_n5_potassium.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, Fig. 9 n5
interp_p27_n5_potassium.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. For an ACE inhibitor the clinician names the potassium result relied on. K is read in mmol/L (no unit is printed). K at most 5.5 permits the order; an unknown K leaves the choice unresolved (format section 5). A CCB or diuretic does not read K. A cited K of 0 mmol/L or less is not a measurement: it is read as an unknown K, so the issue names choice.potassium, the clinician collects it and chooses again. The figure prints no lower K; whether a clinical lower limit applies is a question for Kebba (final review F1). A K result of another patient is an issue: the attributed choice is kept as refused, an evidence review is owned, and the clinician chooses again (final review F2). Review question Q2 (F7).

gap_p27_n21_beta_blocker.note: Source gap. The Fig. 9 remark says to consider beta-blockers "at any treatment step" when there is a specific indication: heart failure, angina, post-MI, atrial fibrillation, or younger women with, or planning, pregnancy. No n4 line names a beta-blocker, and the remark gives no medicine, dose or exit. The draft does not ask for these indications. Each monotherapy choice task names this gap; the clinician may choose no n4 medicine. Open for Kebba: does a planned pregnancy leave the branch like pregnancy (review question 5)? Review F12; independent review M8.

gap_p28_urgency_emergency.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.28, printed p.18, Hypertensive Emergency Management, Definition; PDF p.27, printed p.17, Fig. 9 n3 and n6
gap_p28_urgency_emergency.note: Source gap. PDF p.28 defines hypertensive urgency ("SBP > 180 OR DBP >120 without end-organ damage") and emergency ("> 180/120 plus end-organ damage"). Fig. 9 puts every reading above 150/95 in dual therapy and does not refer to these definitions. The source does not say which passage applies at a health centre, and it gives no management for urgency. The p.24 exception (≥180/110) applies only to the diagnosis. The draft records this gap and no Fig. 9 band, asks for clinical review and orders no medicine. The p.25 work-up is still ordered; the p.28 emergency work-up and management are not encoded. Independent review M7; seed HTN-10.

interp_p12_maximum_intervals.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.12, printed p.2, Fig. 2 and N.B.; studio/decisions/conflict-rbcncd24-screening-interval.json

rbcncd24_p26_targets.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.26, printed p.16, adult hypertension
rbcncd24_p26_targets.note: Figure 8 gives office targets by age and condition. Ages 18–65: systolic 130 or lower if tolerated, not below 120, except the CKD cell. Ages 65–79 and 80 or older: systolic 130–139 if tolerated. All diastolic cells give 70–79. Age 65 overlaps. The CKD cell is not silently repaired.

interp_p26_target_check.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.26, printed p.16, adult hypertension
interp_p26_target_check.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. For the unambiguous non-CKD rows, a tolerated office reading is in target at 120–130/70–79 below age 65, and 130–139/70–79 above age 65. Out-of-range or not-tolerated readings require a clinician treatment decision, never an automatic dose change. The reference leaves exactly 65 and CKD at source gaps.

gap_p26_target_65_ckd.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.26, printed p.16, adult hypertension
gap_p26_target_65_ckd.note: Source ambiguity: the age-65 overlap and CKD cell have active records conflict-rbcncd24-target-at-65 and correction-rbcncd24-fig8-ckd-target in studio/decisions. No clinical resolution is recorded there. The reference does not choose a target for these cases.

interp_p25_followup_review.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.25, printed p.15, adult hypertension
interp_p25_followup_review.note: NEEDS KEBBA REVIEW. A named assessing clinician reviews the office reading, symptoms, organ damage, comorbidities, medicines, adherence, adverse effects, tolerance, renal safety and contraindications. A correlated host assessment attests these findings. This is a draft collection and accountability choice; the national text does not define the electronic form or its completion proof.

gap_p27_longitudinal_excluded.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, adult hypertension

gap_p27_regimen_change.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.27, printed p.17, adult hypertension
gap_p27_regimen_change.note: Incomplete extraction, not absence of national treatment: Figure 9 n12 permits up-titration and its later rows give combination regimens, but the full follow-up change/switch process is not encoded in this reference. In particular, a medicine change is not evidence that the patient already takes the new medicine at a dose above its printed starting amount. The facility must distinguish a new or restarted medicine from titration of the same active prescription, with an explicit proposed SOP.

gap_p12_annual_transition_anchor.locator: RBCNCD24 (library/sources/sources.json rbc-2024-ncd-management-guidelines), PDF p.12, printed p.2, Fig. 2 and annual-screening note
gap_p12_annual_transition_anchor.note: The annual requirement from age 35 also constrains recalls created before 35. The figure does not specify the first eligible appointment anchor. whohtn21_combination.note: WHO suggests combination therapy, preferably a single-pill combination, with classes from thiazide/thiazide-like diuretics, ACE inhibitors/ARBs and long-acting dihydropyridine CCBs. whohtn21_testing.locator: WHOHTN21, PDF p.20 / printed p.8, recommendation 2 and implementation remarks
whohtn21_testing.note: WHO conditionally recommends tests for comorbidity and secondary hypertension without delaying treatment, with low-certainty evidence. If prompt assessment is unavailable, arrange assessment or referral at least as urgent as the most urgent applicable national danger route. Preserve known urgent care and the current safe treatment. Keep missing signs unknown. Do not infer hypertension emergency, change a medicine from an unconfirmed diagnosis, or delay transfer for information.

htn_screening_transition.title: Schedule the first annual screening in the age-35 year
htn_screening_transition.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Cap a pre-35 maximum recall at the measurement anniversary in the first age-35 year: ages 31/32/33/34 use 4/3/2/1 calendar years. This is a proposed appointment anchor, not an inferred birthday or a national exact due date. Imprecise birth data that cannot establish the applicable interval require corrected information. An independent Core workflow keeps the recall executable and starts the next screening from an attributed current reading. A corrected recall keeps its original due instant and measurement anchor. The recall workflow commissions overdue contact once; correcting evidence does not create another contact workflow or complete screening.

htn_screening_definition.title: Use the national diagnostic threshold at the screening boundary
htn_screening_definition.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Use the explicit >=140 systolic OR >=90 diastolic definition across both raised-entry rows. At that boundary, known hypertension symptoms or organ damage reach owned urgent assessment with known, unknown or absent pregnancy. Without danger, known pregnancy retains maternal assessment and unresolved pregnancy cannot enter routine confirmation. Both positive components, office setting and same-patient reading/encounter remain required. This diagnostic boundary does not authorize treatment. The separate emergency choice requests assessment for known concerning signs at any pressure. Split lower categories use the higher component. Keep the source-reference boundary visible. At systolic 160 or diastolic 100 or above, the current register requires clinician diagnosis and treatment assessment now. Lower uncomplicated raised readings retain two-visit confirmation. Diagnosis still requires the clinician.

htn_assessment.title: Keep one accountable clinician for assessment and prescribing
htn_assessment.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Collect a correlated assessment after both the named reading and the current assessment request, and no later than its reporting instant. The next visit needs a different reading and encounter, observed after the previous prescription decision on the date of that visit event, and no later than reporting. These are proposed work/evidence correlation rules, not a maximum clinical age for laboratory evidence. Missing answers and wrong-patient evidence, including the patient attached to each encounter, require corrected evidence. Every assessment and prescription reissue, including invalid, missing and wrong-role answers, keeps the original due instant with a zero-duration offset. Nonpositive BP components are invalid at both screening visits and clinical assessment. An information task captures each candidate second reading before its object is available; an internal ready event evaluates that same candidate after collection. Preserve the original measurement event ID, occurrence, assertion time and transport time in that task and ready event. Known patient-correlated urgent second-visit findings start urgent assessment before diagnostic chronology is checked. Retain duplicate prevention on the candidate collection task, keyed by reading and original evidence occurrence. Correction replies for that same finding keep its request; another finding commissions its own current urgent duty. Diagnostic confirmation cannot close until that candidate has an urgent request. Missing assertion metadata stays unknown with owned correction work. A typed payload.asserted_at must equal the original event time. Native elapsed durations require first observation <= second observation <= original assertion <= transport. Partial replies and corrected references cannot move that clock; a missing or mismatched typed instant requires correction against the retained original time. No minimum visit interval or maximum evidence age is added. Missing or invalid evidence retains owned collection work; collection alone is not diagnosis. Initial and follow-up work share this workflow. The clinician may start amlodipine while the ordered panel remains outstanding, after the safety review; renal and contraindication review remain required, and an ACE inhibitor also requires the named potassium result. No order is treated as a test result.

htn_comorbid_handover.title: Use owned condition-specific care for diabetes and CKD
htn_comorbid_handover.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. The general medicine list cannot replace the national diabetes or CKD algorithm. Until those constraints and exceptions are extracted and reviewed, a named NCD advanced-care clinician must accept the current assessment and next work. CKD target alternatives remain proposed and do not authorize a regimen here.

htn_targets.title: Use the current age-specific target choice
htn_targets.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Proposed: age 65 uses 130–139 systolic for otherwise eligible care. The previously proposed CKD reading a with the hypertension floor retained remains a review alternative only; it is not applied to authorize a general regimen. All CKD and diabetes regimen decisions use an owned condition-specific handover. CKD alternatives remain linked in studio/decisions/correction-rbcncd24-fig8-ckd-target.json. The governing target is conflict-htn-target choice d. A clinician reviews tolerance; stage 4–5 and a stated specialist need have an owned handover.

htn_hc_combination.title: Use the Figure 9 class pairing and doses for a clinician-selected HC combination
htn_hc_combination.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Apply the national ACE inhibitor plus CCB/diuretic pairing at HC/MHC despite the missing n6-to-n10 arrow. Supported ACE inhibitors are enalapril and lisinopril. Do not combine ACE inhibitor and ARB. Initial amounts stay within the printed start amounts. The registered slash reading uses either component above the printed band; both components are above it in the unambiguous 170/100 witness. The initial >150 systolic or >95 diastolic band requires a supported combination or an owned individual-plan handover; ordinary monotherapy cannot bypass it. The task and decision record carry this national indication. The n11 trigger and exact 150/95 boundary retain an explicit clinician choice; no medicine is inferred automatically.

htn_prescription_validity.title: Require a fresh explicit prescription decision
htn_prescription_validity.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. A clinician chooses start, renewal or change and records a reason and validity end. Renewal preserves both medicines and doses of an active same-patient prescription whose validity extends beyond the current Kigali date. A new decision never silently renews an expired prescription. Dispensing must cover the scheduled review and remain within validity.

htn_regimen_change.title: Distinguish medicine switching from titration
htn_regimen_change.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. A new or restarted medicine stays within its printed starting amounts. A dose above that start amount, up to the printed maximum, needs the same medicine on an active, unexpired prescription of this patient. Every increase of a current medicine, including either medicine within a printed starting range, requires pressure above the age-specific target, systolic at least 120, diastolic at least 70 and confirmed tolerance. Below-floor pressure is not above target. A refusal retains owned clinician review and safe current treatment; it never creates a stop order. The clinician explicitly chooses and explains the change after assessment; no titration step or new medicine is inferred. This is a proposed operational reading, not a printed national switching algorithm. Check same-patient current-regimen evidence on every prescribing path, including initial/start. Every known current-medicine increase uses the same pressure, target and tolerance safeguards. One required current_regimen reference names either the active or stopped same-patient prescription or an htn_no_regimen_attestation object. The attestation names this patient, the clinician who completed the assessment and an instant no later than the assessment. It permits only supported first doses in initial/start mode without a prior prescription. An omitted field is not an empty regimen and keeps the assessment unresolved. The facility contract has neither no_current_regimen nor current_prescription. Typed review tasks capture the one reference, so an old inline flag cannot select another branch. Missing or inconsistent prior evidence otherwise keeps immediate owned review or an explicit individual-plan handover. Never infer a stop.

htn_review_intervals.title: Schedule the next clinical review and retain its owner
htn_review_intervals.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Start or change at systolic 160 or diastolic 100 or above: two calendar weeks. Other starts/changes and uncontrolled renewal: four calendar weeks. These follow the current central register, decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Controlled unchanged treatment: three calendar months under conflict-htn-stable-interval. The operational clock starts at the prescription decision, before supply, so failed supply cannot postpone review. This earlier anchor is a local adaptation, not proof that treatment began. An independent ordinary Core workflow owns the clinician-authorized next review. Another owns coordinator contact; both can receive completion after supply or the review finishes. A corrected next-visit request keeps the original due instant and prescription-decision anchor, including after the parent ends. The scheduled-review workflow commissions overdue contact once; corrections before or after due cannot renew the deadline or create another contact workflow. Contact completion does not complete the clinical review.

htn_supply_receipt.title: Separate the prescription, dispensing and patient receipt
htn_supply_receipt.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Pharmacy checks the exact prescription, both medicines and doses, stock, packing and coverage. A two-week prescription needs at least 14 calendar days of coverage through its review, within prescription validity. Insufficient coverage creates immediate owned recovery without moving the review deadline. A separate patient receipt cites the dispensing task and prescription. The actual dispensing instant must follow the current prescription decision and not exceed its reporting instant; receipt must follow that dispensing instant and not exceed its own reporting instant. Event time stays distinct from report time, so delayed reporting is allowed. No stock or failed receipt creates owned recovery; no substitution, renewed prescription or new stop order is inferred. A host-reported failed attempt is cancelled through Core before a replacement can be commissioned. The prescription and coordinator recovery stay open. A failure during an outstanding cancellation request cannot authorize replacement; Core must receive its correlated cancellation acknowledgment. Late reports for a cancelled occurrence remain audited as late and cannot complete supply. The facility correction helper also keeps the prior due instant for timed dispensing, receipt, collection, contact, supply-recovery and handover requests; it never assigns a new deadline from a correction event.

htn_handover.title: Close excluded care only after the named service accepts it
htn_handover.note: Decided by an agent, sign-off pending. Name NCD advanced care, urgent assessment, maternal care or child/adolescent care as appropriate. Exclude pregnancy before routine confirmation. Check current symptoms, organ damage and very-high BP at the second reading before diagnosis work. Carry that current reading, the relevant first/second pair and any diagnostic outcome through the handover and its retries. The coordinator must arrange the handover; the receiving clinician records patient, service and accepted responsibility, with a resolved external next-work object owned by that same clinician and naming the work kind and due instant. That object is external evidence, not a shadow task lifecycle. Requiring the due instant is a proposed handover SOP, not a national time limit. For urgent assessment, accepted next work must be clinical assessment due no later than this acceptance and no earlier than the current urgent request. Acceptance must occur no later than transport receipt. Future or unresolved acceptance keeps immediate owned correction or recovery. Valid delayed reports remain eligible. Later appointments and unrelated work retain immediate owned recovery. This is an operating care duty, not a national transfer-time limit. A refusal stays open. Supply and handover recovery decisions require the coordinator role. A supply handover never fulfils the prescription: its parent remains open for evidence of dispensing and receipt. The local immediate due means start coordination now; it does not claim a national referral deadline or completed transfer. At first office entry with >=140 systolic OR >=90 diastolic and two positive components, known symptoms or organ damage reach owned urgent assessment with known, unknown or absent pregnancy; the no-danger known-pregnancy route remains maternal and unresolved pregnancy cannot enter routine confirmation. The current emergency decision governs receiving-service assessment and treatment, including urgent transfer for concerning symptoms at any pressure. Its hospital regimens remain receiving-service work. The source exact-boundary ambiguity remains visible. Urgent signs at any pressure follow the emergency choice. Assessment does not authorize pregnancy-dependent treatment. Core cancels a host-reported failed handover occurrence before an owned replacement request. A cancelled predecessor cannot remain an outstanding failed duty or count as a later acceptance.
